name: What if a commercial project has multiple stakeholders?

mainEntity.name: How do you manage a commercial project with tenants, owners, landlords, and consultants all involved?
mainEntity.text: How do you manage a commercial project with tenants, owners, landlords, and consultants all involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial projects often have more stakeholders than residential work, and that can create friction if roles are not defined early. The project manager should identify who makes decisions, who reviews plans, who must approve costs, and who only needs updates. A single point of contact helps prevent conflicting instructions and duplicated communication. Regular meetings and written follow-ups keep everyone aligned and reduce misunderstandings. In properties with tenants, landlords, building management, and consultants, the manager also has to protect the project schedule from approval bottlenecks. If stakeholder roles are unclear, small issues can become major delays. Strong project management brings structure to that complexity so the project can move forward efficiently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Multiple stakeholders are managed by creating a clear decision structure, one main point of contact, documented approvals, and regular update meetings. This prevents conflicting directions from slowing the project or causing scope confusion.
